record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Consider a compact connected 2n-dimensional symplectic manifold M, endowed with a Hamiltonian (S1)n- 1-action; these are called complexity one spaces. Consider an integrable system f1,..., fn on M where (f1,..., fn- 1): M → Rn- 1 is the momentum map of the Hamiltonian (S1)n- 1-action. Suppose that the singularities of the integrable s ystem are non-degenerate and also they do not contain hyperbolic blocks. Study how the invariants of the complexity one space are related to the invariants of the semitoric system. For recent progress in the case 2 n = 4 see Hohloch et al [116]. Recently there have been many works on integrable systems which c an be obtained by the method of toric degenerations. In particular, many well-known integrable sys tems can be constructed this way, including the bending flow of 3D polygons Foth et al [77] and the Gelfand-Cetlin 1 system Nishinou et al [174]. See also [113, 130, 175]. A common feature of integrable syste ms coming from toric degenerations is that their base space (the space of fibers of the momentum map) is a convex polytope, which implies that the singular fibers are quite special.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, equipped with an effective Hamiltonian $(S^1)^{n-1}$-action with momentum map $\mu=(f_1,\dots,f_{n-1}):M\to\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$. Such a triple $(M,\omega,\mu)$ is called a complexity one space. Suppose that $f_n:M\to\mathbb{R}$ is a smooth function such that $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ defines a completely integrable system (the components Poisson-commute and are functionally independent on a dense open set). Assume further that every singular point of $F$ is non-degenerate in the Williamson sense and that the local symplectic normal form at each singularity contains no hyperbolic block (so only elliptic and focus–focus blocks occur); call such an $F$ a (higher-dimensional) semitoric system on the complexity one space.

Determine an explicit correspondence between the symplectic invariants of $(M,\omega,\mu)$ as a complexity one space (its Karshon-type combinatorial/graph invariants and equivariant data) and the symplectic invariants of the semitoric system $F$ (such as the number of focus–focus singular fibers, the polygon invariant, the height invariant, the Taylor series invariant at each focus–focus fiber, and the twisting index invariant). In particular, describe how the invariants of $(M,\omega,\mu)$ determine, and are determined by, those of $F$, generalizing the known case $2n=4$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Hohloch–Palmer, Le Floch–Palmer, Alonso–Hohloch, De Meulenaere–Hohloch, and surveys on semitoric systems from 2019–2024) has substantially developed the theory of semitoric invariants in dimension 4, including the twisting index and height invariants, but a general correspondence between complexity one space invariants and semitoric invariants in arbitrary dimension $2n$ has not been established. The problem appears to remain open beyond the 4-dimensional case.

status_evidence.title: Survey on recent developments in semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of the state of the art concerning examples and computations of semitoric invariants reached in 2019.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on semitoric invariants in dimension 4; higher-dimensional correspondence not yet resolved.

status_evidence.title: The twisting index in semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the twisting index invariant of semitoric systems.
status_evidence.claim: Work on individual semitoric invariants continues; general structural correspondence with complexity one data is still under study.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic invariants of semitoric systems and the inverse problem for quantum systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the five symplectic invariants classifying semitoric systems.
status_evidence.claim: Classification framework primarily developed for the 4-dimensional case.
